title: How to Clean a PS5 (Dust and Vents) Without Opening It
hook: Is your PS5 getting loud, hot, or slowing down in long games? Dust is the usual culprit, and you can fix it without opening the console or buying any tools. In seven safe steps, you'll clean the vents, the shell and the controller in about fifteen minutes. Nothing in this video needs tools, and it won't touch your warranty.
intro: Your PS5 pulls air in through its vents and pushes it out through the back. Over months, dust gathers on those openings and inside the fan intake. That makes the fan work harder and louder. The good news is that you only need to clean what you can reach from the outside. You should never open the console's body, unscrew anything, or push objects into the fan. Safety first, and results second. If your console is still under warranty and has a serious problem, contact Sony rather than experimenting.
youNeed: A vacuum with a brush head
youNeedNarration: Here's what you need. A soft, dry microfiber cloth. A clean soft brush, like a paintbrush or a makeup brush. A vacuum cleaner with a soft brush head. A few cotton swabs for tiny gaps. And a slightly damp cloth for stains. Don't use any chemicals, sprays or alcohol on the console. All of these are cheap, and you probably have them at home already.
heroImagePrompt: A white PlayStation 5 console standing on a media shelf in a living room, soft evening light, shallow depth of field, photorealistic, no text

steps.title: Power down and unplug
steps.narration: Step one. Turn the console off completely. Don't use rest mode, because rest mode keeps parts of the console running. Hold the power button until you hear a second beep, or use the power options on the home screen. Then unplug the power cable and every other cable from the back. Let the PS5 cool down for at least thirty minutes if you were playing. Never clean a console that is plugged in or hot, because dust cleaning near live electronics is the main risk in this whole process. Also pull out any disc or game card, and store them away from the dust. A calm, unplugged console is a safe console.
steps.mistake: Cleaning it while it is plugged in
steps.imagePrompt: A hand unplugging a power cable from the back of a white game console, living room shelf, photorealistic, no text

steps.title: Move it to a safe workspace
steps.narration: Step two. Carry the console to a table or workbench with good light, away from carpets and pets. Lay a clean towel under it, so you won't scratch the plastic. If you can, take it outside or near an open window, because dust can fly around in the room. Place a sheet of paper or a bowl nearby for any dust that comes off. Wash and dry your hands, since fingerprints and oils on the shell attract more dust over time. Avoid places with a lot of static electricity, such as thick wool rugs, and wear no loose sleeves that could catch on cables.
steps.imagePrompt: A white game console lying on a folded towel on a wooden table with bright window light, photorealistic, no text

steps.title: Wipe the outside
steps.narration: Step three. Wipe the console's outer shell with a dry microfiber cloth. The glossy black center and the white covers show every fingerprint, and a dry cloth is gentle on them. For marks that remain, dampen the cloth very lightly with water, wring it out, and wipe again, then dry the surface. Never use glass cleaner, alcohol or household sprays, which can damage the finish. Keep the damp cloth away from the ports and vent slots. Take your time around the edges, where dust gathers. A small amount of patience goes a long way here, because the glossy parts scratch easily, so avoid rough fabrics like kitchen towels.
steps.tip: Dry cloth first, damp only if needed
steps.mistake: Using sprays or alcohol on the shell
steps.imagePrompt: A hand wiping a white game console with a soft microfiber cloth, close-up, photorealistic, no text

steps.title: Brush the vents
steps.narration: Step four. Find the vent openings at the back and the top and bottom edges. Using a soft, dry brush, gently sweep the dust off the vent slots, working from the inside edge toward the outside, so the dust falls away instead of being pushed in. Use cotton swabs for the narrow gaps. Don't push anything into the vents, and don't let the brush touch the fan blades. If your console has removable cover plates, your manual shows how they come off without tools, but don't remove anything else. Pay extra attention if you keep your console near a window, a pet bed or a carpeted floor, where dust builds up fastest.
steps.imagePrompt: A soft paintbrush gently sweeping dust from the vent slots of a white game console, macro, photorealistic, no text

steps.title: Vacuum near the openings
steps.narration: Step five. Turn on a vacuum cleaner with a soft brush head, and hold it a few centimetres from each vent, so it pulls the loose dust out. Keep the nozzle close, but not touching the console. Don't push the nozzle into the openings. Go slowly around the intake areas on both sides and the back exhaust. Avoid blasting compressed air into the console, because it can spin the fan too fast, and force dust further inside. If you want more detail, ask a professional, rather than taking the console apart. Go over the area twice, at a slow speed, because dust that is stuck needs a second pass. If your vacuum has several power levels, choose the lowest.
steps.tip: Hold the nozzle just above the vents
steps.mistake: Blasting compressed air into the fan
steps.imagePrompt: A vacuum cleaner soft brush head held just above the vent of a white game console, workshop light, photorealistic, no text

steps.title: Clean ports and the controller
steps.narration: Step six. Look at the USB and HDMI ports. If you see lint, use a dry cotton swab or a soft brush, gently, and don't blow into them. Then wipe the DualSense controller with a slightly damp, well-wrung cloth, including the grips and buttons. Keep moisture away from the charging port, the speaker holes and the triggers. Wipe it dry with a clean cloth. For stubborn dirt between the buttons, use a dry swab. Let everything dry for a few minutes before you reconnect. Let the controller dry fully for ten minutes before using it, because even a little moisture near the sensors can cause problems.
steps.tip: Keep moisture out of the ports
steps.imagePrompt: A cotton swab cleaning the edge of a white game controller next to a microfiber cloth, photorealistic, no text

steps.title: Reconnect and give it space
steps.narration: Step seven. Place the console back where it lives, and make sure it has room to breathe. Leave at least ten centimetres, or four inches, free at the sides and back. Don't put it in a closed cabinet, on a carpet, or next to a heater. Plug in the cables, switch it on, and listen to the fan. Mark your calendar to repeat this every three months, or more often if you have pets. A cleaner PS5 stays cooler, and quieter. If the fan remains loud after cleaning, or the console shuts down by itself with a warning, talk to Sony support.
steps.mistake: Putting it in a closed cabinet
steps.imagePrompt: A white game console on an open shelf with plenty of space around it, TV in the background, photorealistic, no text

mistakesToAvoid.narration: Here are the mistakes to avoid. First, opening the console. It voids your warranty, risks damage, and isn't needed for a basic clean. Second, using liquids, sprays or alcohol on the console, which can seep into the electronics and spoil the finish. And third, cleaning while it is plugged in or hot. Always power it off fully and unplug it first. If your PS5 is still very loud after cleaning, contact Sony support rather than trying something risky. A little regular cleaning always beats a big, risky repair.
items: Using sprays, alcohol or lots of liquid
Cleaning while plugged in or hot

recap.narration: Let's recap. Power down completely and unplug. Move the console to a safe workspace. Wipe the outside. Brush the vents. Vacuum near the openings, without touching them. Clean the ports and the controller. And reconnect it in a spot with plenty of space around it. Seven steps, about fifteen minutes, and a quieter console that stays cooler during long gaming sessions. Keep it simple and gentle, and your PS5 will thank you.
items: Move it to a safe workspace

outro: That's how you clean a PS5 safely, without taking it apart. If your console is quieter now, subscribe to WikiTube, because we publish a new how-to every single day. Tell us in the comments if your PS5 was dusty, and what you would like us to explain next. See you tomorrow.

metadata.title: How to Clean a PS5 (Dust and Vents) Without Opening It
metadata.description:
Is your PS5 loud, hot or full of dust? In this step-by-step video you'll learn how to clean a PS5 safely without opening it: power down and unplug, wipe the shell, brush the vents, vacuum near the openings, clean the ports and the DualSense controller, and give the console room to breathe. No tools, no chemicals, and no risk to your warranty. Also works for PS5 Slim and similar consoles.

You'll need: a soft dry microfiber cloth, a soft brush, a vacuum with a brush head, cotton swabs, a slightly damp cloth.

WikiTube publishes a new step-by-step how-to video every day. Subscribe so you don't miss the next one.
